To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cognitive state of participants with MCI is associated with changes in resting EEG power, coherence, and directed connectivity, and that these changes are related to ApoE status and amyloid burden.
functional and effective connectivities in MCI were reduced compared to healthy controls and were related to age, gender, amyloid deposition and ApoE status.
functional and directed resting state connectivities are associated with neuronal oscillations and are linked to amyloid deposition and ApoE genotype in mild cognitive impairment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an EEG-based biomarker for MCI and AD.
the development of a new biomarker approach to identify early changes of functional and effective connectivities associated with the progression of MCI.
the investigation of neuronal oscillations and functional and directed connectivites in MCI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed alterations in connectivity are related to cognitive decline and may reflect the underlying pathology.
functional and directed connectivity is associated with neuronal oscillations, Apo E genotype and amyloid deposition in MCI.
functional and directed connectivity are sensitive measures for the assessment of cognitive impairment and are related to ApoE genotype and amyloid deposition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of power, coherence and directed connectivity is a promising tool to assess MCI and that the combination of these measures is a promising tool in the context of early AD.
the functional connectivity is more affected by amyloid deposition than the directed connectivities.
functional and directed connectives are sensitive to the MCI state, but are also linked to Apo E genotype and amyloid deposition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analysis of resting-state functional and directed connectives may be a promising approach to assess the progression of MCI.
the assessment of functional and directed connectivity in MCI can provide a better understanding of the neuronal mechanisms underlying cognitive impairment.
the analysis of EEG power and connectivity can be a useful tool in the early detection and diagnosis of cognitive impairment.
